description: This plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing on the Llama2 model after applying different editing methods, comparing accuracy against co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale for values greater than zero, with tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 5 units. The plot contains six solid lines representing different methods, each showing a general upward trend across four data points spanning from just before $10^1$ to just after $10^3$ on the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circular markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 61% and rising steadily to end at roughly 66.5%. The "FT" method, shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, begins at about 62% and increases to approximately 68.5%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting near 64.5% and climbing to about 70.5%. The "MEND" method, indicated by a brown line with diamond markers, starts at approximately 66%, rises to 73.5% at the third data point, and ends slightly higher at roughly 74%. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, beginning at about 66.5%, reaching 72% at the third point, and ending at approximately 72.5%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers; it starts at the highest initial value of approximately 72.5%, increases to about 77.5% at the third data point, and remains steady at 77.5% for the final data point.
